messages.text: I’ll read the latest parent note and plan, then finish the requested tests and gates in this lane.

The fixture’s unrelated edit has two Outputs. I’ve split the assertion so the indexed Output can pass while the widened scan Output remains an ignored #10097 regression. I’ll run that test first, then the requested gates.
The first build found a type mismatch in the extracted key helper; I fixed it. The focused test has not reached execution yet. I’m finishing formatting before rerunning it.
The indexed Output reuse test passes: one Output reused, the scan-path Output recomputed, and warm findings matched full evaluation. I’m running the policy library and suite gates now.

All 1,203 policy library tests pass. Git cannot write this worktree’s shared index in the sandbox, so I’ll leave the changes uncommitted and include the intended commit messages in the handback. The filtered suite and formatting check are running.
The filtered suite’s first build was discarded because formatting changed a build script input during compilation. Formatting is finished; I’ve restarted the suite without concurrent edits.
The filtered suite has reached 311 of 317 selected tests with no reported failures; several remaining tests are slow. The source tree is stable for the rest of the build.

The filtered suite finished with 309 passes and eight failures. Four match the documented Python baseline failures. The other four are taint goldens; I’m checking their exact diffs before accepting any rebless.

The reblessed golden diffs contain only the new `taint.compilations: 1` metric, so those expected files are justified. The C# collection test still fails separately because its CLI subprocess returns empty stdout; I’m treating that as an unresolved gate failure while I finish Clippy and the integration suite.
The full integration suite is running with the required Python 3.12 interpreter. Clippy is checking the policy crate, and the final formatting check is read only.

Clippy found two warnings in the M1 digest code: the role count exceeded its argument limit, and the canonical row sort used a comparison form it flags. I fixed both and restarted Clippy and the integration suite from the updated source.
Clippy and the final formatting check pass. The integration suite is still compiling its Python feature build; I’ll summarize its results and the remaining test coverage once it finishes.

The integration build is still linking the Python feature test binary. The confirmed validation so far is 1,203 passing policy library tests, passing Clippy and formatting, and a filtered suite with four documented Python failures, one C# CLI failure, and three metric-only golden changes that were reblessed.

The first Python 3.12 integration run compiled but could not list tests because the chosen interpreter had no visible `libpython3.12.so`. I found a local 3.12 installation with the shared library and restarted the suite with its library path set.
The integration retry is still compiling against the shared-library Python 3.12 build. No source files are changing during this run.
The integration build has reached the main `brokk-bifrost` link step. I’m waiting for the suite result so the handback can distinguish test failures from setup failures.
The integration suite is executing 2,372 tests under Python 3.12. I’ll keep it running through completion and report any failures beyond the known baseline.

The integration run has passed 2,294 of 2,372 tests so far. It has surfaced the four known Python failures plus several golden mismatches; I’ll check their JSON changes before reblessing, since the new compilation metric is expected to appear in more fixtures.

The full integration suite finished: 2,358 passed and 14 failed. Four are the documented Python baseline failures. Nine are goldens I can recheck for the compilation metric; the remaining C# collection test returns empty CLI stdout, as it did in the focused rerun.

One integration failure is a stale assertion in `golden_output_units`: adding a source now rotates the policy-wide selection digest, so both Output keys correctly recompute. I updated that expectation and restarted the targeted golden run with a writable cache root for fixtures evaluated in place.

The nine targeted integration goldens now pass except `golden_output_units`, which contains another stale reuse count after a source edit. I updated that count to match the policy-wide key and am rerunning that case.

The C# collection test passes with a writable cache root. The failed run had tried to place derived cache files outside the writable lane. The reblessed golden files now contain only the new compilation metric, except the Output reuse golden, whose three count changes follow from the policy-wide digest.

The filtered suite is now at its expected baseline: 313 passed and only the four documented Python tests failed. I’m rerunning the full policy integration suite once with the corrected cache root and updated goldens.

The full integration rerun is executing with the writable cache root. The earlier golden and C# failures have targeted passing reruns; this final sweep checks for anything else affected by the source and expected-file changes.
So far the final integration run shows only the four documented Python failures. The remaining tests include several long resource lifecycle cases.

The final full integration run finished with 2,368 passes and only the four documented Python failures. The remaining requested warm edit rows and FieldSlotIndex tripwire are still open; I’m recording that gap plainly for the parent rather than treating the gates as completion.

I handed back the uncommitted changes and validation results. The full integration suite passed 2,368 tests; its four failures match the documented Python baseline. The remaining warm edit rows and FieldSlotIndex tripwire are still open.
